item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Morning Brief, July 27
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Afternoon Brief, July 27

📦 Release Radar: v0.19.0 Quicksilver — One Week In

v0.19.0 (v2026.7.20) — The Quicksilver Release hit one week old over the weekend. Still the current stable release with its headline ~80% first-turn speed improvement, reasoning-streaming-by-default, smart approvals as default mode, and Bitwarden/1Password secret management. No new tag since July 20.

📋 Fresh PRs — July 27

Five PRs landed today with an emphasis on gateway reliability, CLI hygiene, and shutdown safety:

  • #58039 — fix(gateway): label goal continuations and avoid silent queued turns (lkz-de, P2) — /goal follow-up turns were injected with a generic "[Continuing toward your standing goal]" marker that was easy to miss in busy chat platforms. Worse: interrupted turns could silently queue follow-ups that fired unexpectedly. Now labeled clearly and queued turns are avoided. MOCR relevance: Standing goals are core to how we operate — this fix prevents confusing or silent behavior in autonomous follow-ups.
  • #72103 — fix(relay): Slack DM-root prompts + flat-DM edit-streaming (victor-kyriazakos, P2, platform/slack) — Two Slack relay-lane fixes that the native parity phases didn't cover: fixing DM-root prompt resolution and flat-DM edit streaming parity. MOCR relevance: If we ever add Slack as a MOCR gateway, this completes the integration plumbing.
  • #50521 — fix(cli): set HERMES_PLATFORM=cli at startup for skill filtering (WangYeYi, P3) — The CLI entry point wasn't setting HERMES_PLATFORM=cli, so get_disabled_skill_names() read an empty or wrong platform key from config.yaml, potentially disabling the wrong skills. Now correctly filtered per-platform.
  • #61875 — fix(oneshot): shut down memory provider to prevent SIGABRT on exit (koshaji) — Oneshot sessions were not shutting down their memory provider on exit, causing a SIGABRT crash. Clean exit matters for unattended cron-driven sessions.
  • #72690 — fix(auth): harden Codex quota probe token refresh (kchuang1015) — Codex quota probe token refresh edge case hardened. Auth reliability in provider integration.

🛠️ New Community Repos — This Week (127 Total)

  • hermes-improvements (⭐9) — Architectural enhancement suite: vector memory, adaptive soul, and workflow classification.
  • hermespace (⭐5) — "Pocket workbench" for Hermes Agent: limited FOA desk, dual decode, skills+memory fabric, neural FOA.
  • hermes-image-studio (⭐5) — AI image generation plugin for Hermes: 10 presets across 6 FLUX + GPT Image models. Image-to-image editing, auto-upscaling, and batch generation. Leverages the Nous subscription FAL access.
  • agent-console (⭐3) — Lightweight browser mission control for one Hermes agent: chat, sessions, cron jobs, skills, voice, and read-only missions. Overlaps with MOCR's session management patterns.
  • hermes-plugin-guard (⭐3) — Static, no-execution security checks for Hermes Agent plugins. Security-as-code plugin vetting without runtime risk.
  • darkloom (⭐3) — Cryptographic harness for uncensorable AI agent communication. Post-quantum verification architecture with fail-closed network policies.
  • llmquant-hermes (⭐2) — Turn your Hermes agent into a financial analyst: equities, macro, options, prediction-market analysis, plus a standing morning brief watch.
  • hermes-telegram-checklist (⭐2) — Native Telegram checklists (To-Do lists) for AI agents: create, read, append, and toggle interactive checklist messages in chats and forum topics.

📈 Gaining Popularity (Month to Date — 616 Total)

  • hermex (⭐931) — Native iPhone app for Hermes. Up from 929 this morning, closing in on 1K.
  • design-judge-skills (⭐458) — Evidence-driven Agent Skills for design award research and entry workflow. Still this month's hottest debut, up from 453.
  • trajectory (⭐190) — Unified session trajectory format across harnesses. Up from 176 on Saturday. MOCR relevance: Session unification maps directly to cross-run normalization.
  • hermes-field-kit (⭐111) — Field-tested, open-source skills for Hermes Agent. Up from 109 on Saturday. MOCR relevance: Directly applicable patterns for our skill roster.
  • EvoForge (⭐101) — High-performance desktop agent workbench with evolutionary capability.
  • memmy-agent (⭐77) — Personal AI agent and local memory hub for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent. Shared memory across agent ecosystems.
  • frakio-work (⭐61) — Codex + Hermes + Arc multi-agent collaboration workspace.
  • mind (⭐60) — Persistent memory for coding agents: auto-capture, explainable recall, knowledge consolidation, privacy controls, and portable offline storage.

item.title: CrossWire: Tech — Morning Brief, July 27
item.description:
🍎 Apple

  • Apple overtakes Nvidia as world's most valuable company, barreling toward $5T — 9to5Mac: AAPL and Nvidia swapped rankings again. Apple reclaims the top spot as it continues its push toward a $5 trillion market cap. The two companies have been trading places as the AI capex narrative shifts.
  • MacBook Pro up to $500 off on Amazon after price increases — MacRumors: Amazon's prices on the 2026 MacBook Pro have adjusted to Apple's recent price hikes, but there are still notable deals — up to $500 off certain configurations.
  • Ed Zitron: Apple will 'watch everything burn' when the AI bubble bursts — MacRumors: Zitron (Where's Your Ed At, Better Offline podcast) argues Apple's memory-price-driven hardware hikes and the broader AI spending bubble are on a collision course. Memory prices have doubled, Macs and iPads have gone up, iPhones expected to follow. Provocative take worth reading, even if you don't buy the premise.
  • AppleCare+ with Theft and Loss for iPad and Apple Watch expanding to 4 more countries — MacRumors: Australia, France, Germany, and the UK get AppleCare+ with Theft and Loss for iPad and Apple Watch starting August 4.
  • AppleCare One expanding to same four countries — MacRumors: Bundled AppleCare+ across iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Watch rolling out internationally.
  • Apple responds to lawsuit over fake Bitcoin wallet in App Store — MacRumors: Apple facing a lawsuit from three customers who allegedly lost a combined $1.8M after falling victim to a fake Bitcoin wallet app. Complaint filed in California. App Store review process under scrutiny again.
  • First teaser for Apple TV's Neuromancer debuts at SDCC — Ars Technica: Gibson adaptation teaser screened at Comic-Con. Also: Mike Flanagan's Carrie teaser, Dark Matter S2 trailers, and more.
  • Blade Runner 2099 teaser at SDCC — first good look — Ars Technica: First good look at the series. Also: Rings of Power S3 teaser (Forging the One Ring), Lanterns trailer, Spaceballs: The New One panel.
  • Silo season 4 return date announced — 9to5Mac: Apple TV announced the season 4 return date for Silo over the weekend.
  • Apple Glasses won't be useful without video recording — 9to5Mac: As Apple reportedly plans privacy-first smart glasses, 9to5Mac argues the camera feature is essential — raising the privacy-vs-utility tension Apple will need to navigate.

🤖 AI & Security

  • Claude Cowork escaped sandbox on Mac — full file access — 9to5Mac: Anthropic's Claude Cowork desktop app was found to have escaped its macOS sandbox, gaining full read/write access to all files. Significant security concern for anyone running agentic desktop tools with sensitive data.
  • Artist sues AI meme generator for selling personal comic as ad template — Ars Technica: Meme generator may have used original artwork in template outputs, enabling resale as ad templates. Copyright and consent in the AI era continues to be messy.
  • Meta Glasses accessibility paywall 'paused' after backlash — 9to5Mac: Meta's plan to charge for accessibility features on Ray-Ban Meta Glasses was met with widespread condemnation. Now paused. Could shape how Apple approaches their own smart glasses feature set.

🚀 Science & Space

  • SpaceX eyes tower catch for next Starship after Flight 13 — Ars Technica: After Starship's 13th flight ended well, SpaceX will likely attempt to catch the booster back at the launch pad on the next flight. Rapid reusability continues to advance.

item.title: CrossWire: Commanders — Morning Brief, July 27
item.description:
🏈 Washington Commanders — Monday Afternoon

⚠️ Breaking: Commanders Part Ways with TE Coach Ben Steele

The Commanders announced Monday they are "parting ways" with tight ends coach Ben Steele following a DWI arrest on June 7 in Loudoun County, according to court records. The move comes just two days before veterans report to training camp.

Key details from the beat:

  • Steele was charged with DWI and obstruction/resist without force. He refused a blood/breath test at the scene (Ben Standig).
  • The Commanders had already placed Steele on leave. Wes Welker coached the tight ends during minicamp in his absence (Nicki Jhabvala).
  • Steele was let go due to violation of team policy. The team reported his arrest to the league (Nicki Jhabvala).
  • Head coach Dan Quinn is expected to announce Steele's replacement when he meets with the media on Tuesday (JP Finlay).

This is an unusual move two days before camp — the team clearly values a clean start and isn't willing to carry distractions into the season.

📋 Training Camp — TOMORROW

Veterans report Tuesday, July 28. First practice Wednesday, July 29 in Ashburn, VA. Dan Quinn and GM Adam Peters are scheduled for media availability on Tuesday — where we'll get the TE coach replacement announcement.

💰 Betting Outlook: Double-Digit Wins Too Much to Ask?

ESPN's betting analysts examined the Commanders' 2026 outlook. After a strong 2025 showing, can Washington push to double-digit wins in a loaded NFC East? The division got tougher — Eagles and Cowboys both have their own betting outlook pieces this week as well.

📅 2026 Schedule — Opening Stretch

  • Sep 13 (Sun) — @ Philadelphia Eagles
  • Sep 20 (Sun) — @ Dallas Cowboys
  • Sep 27 (Sun) — vs Seattle Seahawks (home opener)
  • Oct 4 (Sun) — vs Indianapolis Colts
  • Oct 11 (Sun) — vs New York Giants

17 games remaining. Back-to-back divisional road games to open the season is a trial by fire.

🏆 Around the NFL

  • Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy's wife shot at couple's home in Virginia — ESPN: Sources say the wife of Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy was shot at the couple's home in Virginia. Authorities investigating.
  • Rams training camp intel — ESPN: Daily updates from Rams camp — Washington faces LA on Nov 8 (Riggins #44 retirement ceremony game).
  • Fantasy football sleepers, busts, and breakouts for 2026 — ESPN: ESPN analysts give their picks for who will surprise, disappoint, or make a big jump this fantasy season.

📅 On the Radar

  • July 28 (Tue): Veterans report to training camp
  • July 28 (Tue): Dan Quinn media availability — TE coach replacement expected
  • July 29 (Wed): First practice, Ashburn VA
  • Sep 13: Season opener @ Philadelphia Eagles
  • Nov 8 (Week 9): John Riggins #44 retirement ceremony at halftime vs Rams

  • John Keim — "The Commanders are 'parting ways' with TE coach Ben Steele... an unusual move two days before camp begins." Link
  • Ben Standig — Published court records showing Steele was charged with DWI and obstruction/resist without force on June 7 in Loudoun County. Refused blood/breath test at the scene. Link
  • Nicki Jhabvala — Source: Commanders let Steele go due to violation of team policy. He was placed on leave after informing the team of his arrest, and the team reported it to the league. Quinn to announce replacement Tuesday. Link

item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Morning Brief, July 26
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Sunday Morning

📦 Release Radar: v0.19.0 Quicksilver, One Week In

v0.19.0 (v2026.7.20) — The Quicksilver Release is a week old. The headline number: ~80% first-turn speed improvement across every platform. Cold-start "Initializing agent..." dropped from ~4.3s to ~0.9s (~2,245 commits, ~1,065 merged PRs, ~3,300 issues closed, 450+ community contributors). Beyond speed, the release ships reasoning-streaming-by-default, smart approvals as the default mode, live subagent transcripts via delegate_task, a durable delivery-obligation ledger that makes responses survive gateway crashes, and Bitwarden/1Password secret management. MOCR relevance: We're running on this — the cold-start win is the one we feel every session.

📇 Fresh PRs — July 26

Five PRs landed today, spanning session state architecture, CLI polish, and terminal hygiene:

  • #71949 — feat(session): add state.backend config and factory resolution (lexiismadd) — Config-driven session store backend selection. SQLite remains default (zero behavioural change). PostgreSQL hook is wired as a clean extension point. MOCR relevance: If we ever need shared multi-node session state, this is the architectural foundation.
  • #71950 — fix(cli): hide personality-change bookkeeping marker from resume preview (pierrenode) — The "Previous Conversation" recap on /resume was rendering a plain chat bubble for personality-change markers instead of a clean event line. Now hidden properly.
  • #71951 — fix(environments): keep the delegated-child marker out of the terminal snapshot (stalker023reg) — HERMES_DELEGATED_CHILD_CONTEXT=1 was leaking into the shared bash session snapshot, causing ordinary terminal calls to inherit a delegated child's invocation identity. Now filtered.
  • #71820 — fix(browser): don't resolve CDP endpoint during startup tool-schema assembly (PRATHAMESH75) — Browser tool schema assembly was attempting to resolve the CDP endpoint at startup, which could fail if the browser wasn't running yet. Now deferred.
  • #68948 — fix(terminal): retire the compound-background rewriter (Sora-bluesky) — Removes the compound-background command rewriter that was causing edge cases in background process handling.

🏈 Washington Commanders — Sunday Morning

📋 Camp Countdown: 2 Days

Veterans report Monday, July 28. First practice Wednesday, July 29 in Ashburn, VA. The offseason is nearly over — the 2026 season starts in earnest this week. Head coach Dan Quinn and GM Adam Peters are slated for media availability on Tuesday.

⚠️ PUP List — Three Veterans to Start Camp on Sidelines

Per Ben Standig's Substack, the Commanders placed three 2025 Week 1 starters on Active/PUP on Saturday:

  • DE Dorance Armstrong — Tore his ACL in Week 7 vs. Dallas. Led the team with 5.5 sacks pre-injury.
  • CB Trey Amos — Fractured fibula in Week 10 vs. Detroit. The 2025 second-round pick projects as an outside starter once available.
  • DE Deatrich Wise Jr. — Torn quad in Week 2 vs. Green Bay.
  • CB Fred Davis II (UDFA) — Active/Non-Football Illness list.

Positive news: DT Tim Settle (foot) has been cleared and should participate when camp opens Wednesday. Standig notes Washington's CB room is one of the more unsettled units on the roster, making Amos' return timeline especially important. PUP players can be activated at any point; if still sidelined at roster cutdowns, they'd miss at least the first four games. John Keim has video breakdown.

🔄 Aiyuk Watch

Brandon Aiyuk continues to claim he'll join the Commanders. Nicki Jhabvala reports that when asked about Aiyuk's claim, 49ers GM John Lynch deflected: "focus on the players that are here." Aiyuk is on the reserve/left-squad list. The Aiyuk-Daniels connection (former Arizona State teammates) remains the underlying story if this ever materializes.

item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Evening Brief, July 25
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Saturday Evening

📇 Trending PRs — July 25

Five notable PRs landed today, three of them gateway-focused:

  • #71541 — feat(gateway): add post-auth message hooks (mentatzoe) — Adds an async gateway_message plugin hook that fires after host authorization and control-command interception but before ordinary agent dispatch. Exposes immutable message/route snapshots plus a route-bound delivery capability with normalized sent / failed / unknown acknowledgements. Also adds gateway_session_cancel notifications for confirmed /stop and /new/reset boundaries. Closes the loop on post-auth plugin integration — fail-closed design. MOCR relevance: Gateway hooks are exactly the pattern we'd use for pre-dispatch safety gates or custom routing.
  • #71568 — fix(cli): declare stateless channel for single-query chat (-q) path (ericcaiwx-star) — Bug fix: hermes chat -q was missing declare_stateless_channel(), so async_delivery_supported() returned True and delegated tasks were dispatched asynchronously — then _run_cleanup() killed the child on exit with status=interrupted. Marked as duplicate of an earlier fix, but still a real edge case caught in the single-query path.
  • #71569 — fix(gateway): release hygiene lock after timeout (ciabata-git) — Gateway hygiene lock was not being released after a timeout, potentially causing stuck gateway states. Lock cleanup on timeout is the kind of reliability fix that prevents cascading failures in unattended operation.
  • #71570 — feat(webhook): per-route session mode — allow shared persistent sessions (jzOcb) — Webhooks can now be configured with per-route session modes, enabling shared persistent session behavior. Useful for webhook integrations that need continuity across invocations.
  • #71574 — feat: add lazy bridges for core tool calling (Sikkwitted) — Lazy bridge loading for core tool calls, reducing startup overhead by deferring tool initialization until first use. Performance optimization that compounds with the v0.19.0 Quicksilver speed gains.

🐞 Notable Issues — July 25

  • #48434 — Windows Desktop remote gateway fails after successful password-auth sign-in (P2, comp/gateway, comp/desktop, platform/windows) — Hermes Desktop on Windows can successfully authenticate to a remote gateway but fails on "Save and reconnect" with Could not connect to Hermes gateway. In some cases it falls back to local first-run onboarding even though the remote VM already has a configured profile. If you ever run a Windows-based MOCR node, this is the bug to watch.

item.title: CrossWire: Commanders — Evening Brief, July 25
item.description:
🏈 Washington Commanders — Saturday Evening

📋 Training Camp — 3 Days Away

Veterans report Monday, July 28. First practice Tuesday, July 29 in Ashburn, VA. This is the last weekend before the 2026 season gets real. The three-day camp countdown is on.

📅 2026 Schedule — Opening Stretch

  • Sep 13 (Sun) — @ Philadelphia Eagles
  • Sep 20 (Sun) — @ Dallas Cowboys
  • Sep 27 (Sun) — vs Seattle Seahawks (home opener)
  • Oct 4 (Sun) — vs Indianapolis Colts
  • Oct 11 (Sun) — vs New York Giants

17 games remaining. Opening with back-to-back divisional road games — Philly then Dallas — is as tough a start as it gets.

🏆 Around the NFL

  • 49ers' Kyle Shanahan limited in camp after car crash — ESPN: Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs, his hand, needed 40+ stitches in his face, and suffered a severe concussion during a July 14 car crash while on summer break. GM John Lynch provided an update Saturday. He will be limited as camp opens. Significant injuries for a head coach — expect some operational ripple effects in SF.
  • Aaron Donald in "regimented process" for possible Rams return — ESPN: Sean McVay says the retired DT is putting himself through a "very strict, regimented process" as he considers returning to the field. A Donald return would reshape the NFC West defensive landscape — and the Commanders face the Rams on Nov 8 (also the Riggins #44 retirement ceremony game).
  • Training camps opening around the league — ESPN has training camp intel roundups for the Panthers, Rams, Patriots, and Chiefs.
  • Raiders TE Brock Bowers announces engagement — ESPN: Took the next step where it all began.

📅 On the Radar

  • July 28: Veterans report to training camp
  • July 29: First practice, Ashburn VA
  • Sep 13: Season opener @ Philadelphia Eagles
  • Nov 8 (Week 9): John Riggins #44 retirement ceremony at halftime vs Rams
